chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Zurarah, who said:
I heard him (peace be upon him) say: 'There is no harm in a man marrying a Jewish woman or a Christian woman for temporary marriage (mut'ah), provided he already has a wife.'

key_terms.وَعِنْدَهُ: and with him is / provided he has

ai.seo_question: Can a Muslim man marry a Jewish or Christian woman for temporary marriage while already having a wife?
ai.summary: This narration from the *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* confirms the permissibility of *mut'ah* (temporary marriage) with *Kitabiyyat* (chaste Jewish or Christian women), a ruling distinct from permanent marriage restrictions. It specifically notes that this applies even if the man already has a permanent wife, reflecting the Shia view that *mut'ah* does not carry the same polygyny limits as *nikah al-da'im*. This highlights the flexibility of temporary contracts in Shia jurisprudence regarding interfaith unions.
